chunks: Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn ʿĪsā, from ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥakam, from Abān and al-Ḥusayn ibn Saʿīd, from Faḍālah, from Ḥusayn, from Ibn Miskān, all together from Abī al-ʿAbbās, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:

I asked him about the ghusl (ritual bath) of the deceased, and he said: “Sit him up and press his stomach with a gentle pressing, then cleanse him of what comes out from pressing the stomach. Then lay him down, then wash him, beginning with his right sides, and wash him with water and lote, then with water and camphor, then wash him with pure water, and place him in his shrouds.”
Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥasan said: What this report contains in his statement, “Sit him up,” is not acted upon, and the reason in it is taqiyyah, due to its conformity with the doctrines of the generality.

key_terms.التَّقِيَّةُ: dissimulation or precautionary conformity to protect oneself
key_terms.الْحُرُضِ: lote or cleansing herb mixed with water for washing
key_terms.غُسْلِ الْمَيِّتِ: the ritual washing of the deceased
key_terms.كَافُورٍ: camphor used in one stage of washing the deceased

ai.seo_question: What does this hadith say about how to perform the ghusl of the deceased in Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām?
ai.summary: This hadith discusses the procedure for the ghusl (ritual bath) of the deceased, including the order of washing and the substances used. It also includes a note from Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥasan stating that the instruction to sit the deceased up is not acted upon and is understood as taqiyyah because it accords with the views of the generality.
